title: Date-aligned macro-lattice sweep (sp500) — second-window validation of F17
recipe: matched xgb mcw=10 single-fit; base(all) vs macro(all_macro); only candidates differ — identical to _263 except the split
headline: VALIDATION FAILS. On the independent date-aligned window the _263 trailing top-of-book macro edge does NOT replicate: of 12 cells testable in both windows, only 4/12 agree in sign at R-p@1, 8/12 FLIP. The biggest trailing winners flip hardest (+20%/50d +0.30->-0.11; +50%/50d +0.14->0.00; +20%/25d +0.09->-0.04). Net macro effect on date_aligned is ~neutral (@1 mean +0.004, 5 help / 8 hurt). Only the low-threshold +10% cells help consistently.
verdict: Macro is NOT a robust, deployable edge. The _262/_263 win was window-specific. Reaffirms the _258-_261 'contextually additive but not robust' conclusion with a clean two-window view. DO NOT wire macro into /daily-predictions. date_aligned succeeded at its mechanical goal (all long-horizon cells now testable, Q=100).
